scope: project evidence promoted to cross-agent canonical practice
user_decision: The owner approved the comparison-board layout as the project standard and requested that the practice be captured for later curation into the canonical agent. In the follow-up on 2026-10-04, the owner explicitly asked to make roster-wide concept harmony a permanent agent attention and requested a measured sprite-scale/morphology workflow.

evidence.role: front/side concept comparison using one shared relative display ruler
one existing frame per character; native colors/pixels preserved; x5 nearest-neighbor and common baseline
reference paths, SHA-256 values, frame sizes and review status

proposed_practices: Keep concept-art comparison and existing-sprite comparison as separate boards.
Use a common canvas, labeled character cards, consistent baselines and one relative ruler; state clearly that display units are not canonical heights.
Choose one existing source frame per sprite sheet; crop transparent margins only, enlarge by an integer nearest-neighbor factor, align baselines and disclose native cell and visible-pixel dimensions.
Do not repaint, recolor or otherwise normalize source sprite pixels for the comparison board.
Use approved project art only as a rendering-treatment reference; use each character game source and approved palette as the authority for identity and color.
Preserve source assets; confine background removal or isolated-fragment cleanup to derived review compositions and disclose those edits.
Mark generated turnaround studies as proposals and keep them out of runtime assets until separately reviewed and approved.
Store reference paths, hashes, transforms and review status in a manifest so later reviewers can reproduce the comparison.

future_curation.candidate_workflow: Promoted as L105 with a roster measurement tool and workflow/skill guidance; artistic morphology and rendering still require human review.
future_curation.measurement_boundary: Automate manifest completeness, file existence, hashes, frame extraction, scale and baseline metadata; human review remains necessary for artistic harmony and fidelity.
